concerns.text: The Sparse Autoencoder is trained on the *intersected* ROCStories subset (T050.4) and later the same intersected story set is used for RSA evaluation (T036). This creates a circularity / double‑dipping problem because the model is evaluated on data it was trained on, inflating similarity measures and invalidating the claim that the architecture yields more brain‑like representations.

The pipeline only requires a minimum of 10 shared stories (T023.1) to proceed. Ten items provide extremely low statistical power for RSA and permutation testing, making it unlikely to detect meaningful differences between models and increasing false‑negative risk.

The permutation test convergence criterion (variance < 0.001 over the last 1 000 permutations) is used as a proxy for sufficient power, but without a priori power analysis or a larger sample size this does not guarantee that the test can reliably detect the expected effect size.
